archetypes.name: bash-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan ports specific bash constructs and cites exact line ranges in lint-fix-loop.sh and run-relevant-checks-captured.sh; a reviewer must cross-check those citations against the real bash originals to catch silent behavioral divergence before implementation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify whether the plan's Python behavior descriptions match the bash originals it claims to port. Check the codex/cursor dispatch argv shapes the plan attributes to lint-fix-loop.sh:234-310, 245-252, and 290-296 against the actual bash source. Verify the loop accounting transitions (applied/no-changes/main-agent-required/failed and the consecutive-empty-failure rule) against run_captured_cmd_then_fix_loop in lint-fix-loop.sh. Check whether the coverage/phase log markers the plan expects to parse match what run-relevant-checks-captured.sh actually emits. Flag any plan claim about bash behavior that is not supported by the cited source, and any default or cap value (e.g. RCC_MAX_ITER_DEFAULT, the 60000-byte tail bound) that diverges from the bash originals. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sibling-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan calls specific functions from python/ sibling modules by name; a mismatch between plan-cited names and actual module exports means checks.py will fail at import or call time, which no unit test can catch until the module is written.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine whether every sibling-module reference in the plan matches the actual exported names and signatures in the python/ directory. Check agents.classify_launch_failure, is_transient_infra_failure, git.rev_parse, git.status, git.reset, outcomes.StepResult, outcomes.Outcome, redact.redact, and config.RCC_MAX_ITER_DEFAULT against what those modules actually expose. Verify the plan's stated exclusion of agents.build_launch_argv, agents.launch_tier, and agents.run_waterfall is consistent with the actual roles those functions serve. Assess whether the plan's decision to invoke git verbs (diff --name-only, add, checkout --, merge-base --is-ancestor) through the raw Runner rather than extending git.py creates an abstraction inconsistency with the established git.py pattern. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: test-gap
archetypes.rationale: The plan lists many test cases but may not cover every behavioral state in the plan body; gaps here let parity-critical behaviors (forbidden-path reversion, redaction invariant, dispatch-argv shape) ship without a safety net.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each behavioral state and transition described in the plan body — including every escalate() outcome mapping, the codex-then-cursor dispatch-argv parity shape, the forbidden-path reversion paths for both committed-delta and working-tree cases, the redaction-before-prompt invariant, the skipped/fail-closed script-detection logic, both dual-mode loop shapes (check-first and dispatch-first), the consecutive-empty-failure rule, and the head-changed ancestry guard — verify that the testing strategy section contains at least one explicit test case. Identify any plan-described behavior that has no corresponding test case and assess whether the gap is significant enough to require a new test before implementation proceeds. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
